options.denominator: Equal 12-hour clock-time periods (7am–6:59pm versus 7pm–6:59am), summed across all dates
options.reason: Crash totals show the volume of reported incidents that each time window contributes to the overall burden.
options.answer: Across 2012-07-01 to 2026-06-11, there were 1,543,368 day crashes versus 725,819 night crashes, but these totals do not establish per-trip danger because traffic exposure is unavailable.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how many reported crashes occurred in equal-length daytime and nighttime windows; the chart shows lower total crash volume at night. It is defensible as an incident-burden comparison, but it leaves unanswered whether an individual road user faces greater risk at night because vehicle, pedestrian, and trip exposure are not measured.

options.metric: Share of reported crashes with any injury or any fatality
options.denominator: All reported crashes with a recorded crash time in the corresponding day/night period
options.grouping: Day versus night; injury and fatality outcomes shown separately
options.reason: Outcome shares compare the severity of a reported crash while accounting for the different numbers of crashes in each period.
options.answer: Night crashes were more severe per reported crash: 28.1% involved an injury versus 23.0% by day, and 0.268% involved a death versus 0.099%, but missing traffic exposure prevents a per-trip danger conclusion.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether a reported crash is more likely to involve injury or death at night; the chart shows higher shares for both outcomes at night, by 5.1 percentage points for injury and 2.7 times the fatal-crash share. It is defensible as a comparison of crash severity conditional on a crash being reported, but it leaves unanswered the chance of a crash per trip, mile, or person out at night.
